headline: NASDAQ **-10.4%**
IN ONE WEEK
cover.hook_pick_reason: No reader-impact hook: heise online reports index moves and the open question about AI spending, but states no effect on ordinary readers' pensions, funds, prices or jobs, so a 'your pension' hook would promise something the slides cannot support. The headline pairs the Nasdaq 100's 10.4% weekly loss, a hard number from heise, with a clear time frame, and slides 2-5 cover the week, the bear-market label, Nvidia, and Taiwan. 'Nvidia -14%' is narrower and risks implying wrongdoing. The Taiex option is strong for the Asia angle but names a less familiar index. The bear-market claim is accurate only when attributed to Bloomberg and the FT, which the cover cannot do.

slides.title: US tech stocks had a brutal week
body: The Nasdaq 100, the tech-heavy US index, lost **10.4%** this week. The broader S&P 500 fell 8.6%. Friday alone was sharp: the Nasdaq 100 closed down 5.61% and the S&P 500 down 3.70%.

slides.title: Bloomberg and FT say bear market
body: Bloomberg and the Financial Times now call the Nasdaq 100 a bear market. Their evidence is a **20% drop** from its most recent high in October.

slides.title: Nvidia shares are down 39% this month
body: Nvidia closed Friday **14% lower** after Reuters reported that US market regulators are investigating the chipmaker. What is being investigated was not disclosed, and Nvidia declined to comment. An investigation alone does not indicate misconduct.

slides.title: Taiwan's market fell even harder
body: The Taiex, the index of companies listed on Taiwan's stock exchange, lost **17.5%** this week. The selloff was not only an American story.

slides.title: From AI euphoria to doubt
body: Instead of big AI euphoria, the question now is whether AI makers **spend and borrow too much** to ever turn a profit, heise online reports.

facts.text: The tech-heavy stock index Nasdaq 100 lost 10.4 percent of its points over the course of the week; the broader S&P 500 fared little better with a weekly loss of 8.6 percent.
The Nasdaq 100 closed the day (Friday, 20 November) down 5.61 percent; the S&P 500 went into the weekend with a daily loss of 3.70 percent.
This made the Nvidia share price drop by 39 percent this month.
As the news agency Reuters reported on Friday, US market regulators are investigating Nvidia. After this became known, the share closed Friday down 14 percent.
Taiex, the index of companies traded on the Taiwanese stock exchange, lost 17.5 percent this week.
Bloomberg and the Financial Times now speak of a bear market for the Nasdaq 100, citing as evidence the 20 percent price loss since the most recent high in October.
An investigation alone is not yet an indicator of misconduct. What exactly is investigated was not disclosed; Nvidia declined to comment.
Instead of the big AI euphoria, the question is now whether AI makers spend and borrow too much money to end up profitable.

sources.title_en: Nvidia comes under further pressure – and US tech stocks into a bear market

caption:
The Nasdaq 100 lost 10.4% in one week as Nvidia and AI stocks sank.

heise online reports Taiwan's market fell even harder, and Bloomberg and the Financial Times now call the Nasdaq 100 a bear market.

→ The Nasdaq 100 fell 10.4% this week and the S&P 500 fell 8.6%; Friday alone cost 5.61% and 3.70%
→ Nvidia shares are down 39% this month, 14% on Friday after Reuters reported a US regulator probe; what is investigated is undisclosed, and an investigation alone does not indicate misconduct
→ Taiwan's Taiex lost 17.5% this week, and the question now is whether AI makers spend and borrow too much to be profitable

Is this a healthy reset or the start of something bigger for AI?

Source: heise online, "Nvidia comes under further pressure – and US tech stocks into a bear market" (in German), Nov 22, 2026.
